newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasuries end mixed erasing earlier losses.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries end mixed erasing earlier losses.

text.p: The prices of U.S. Treasury securities closed narrowly mixed on Friday after erasing large losses seen early in the session. The short end outperformed the coupon sector as stocks fell sharply.

Treasuries had ended sharply higher on Thursday following the release of data suggesting inflation remained well contained in July. Dealers said the runup may have been overdone leading to a corrective move this session.
No substantial data releases were scheduled over the next two weeks and range-bound trading was expected, analysts said.

The Federal Reserve's policy-making Federal Open Market Committee meets on Tuesday, but analysts said any further tightening of monetary policy was highly unlikely given the lack of inflationary pressures seen in July.

The Fed last ratcheted up short-term interest rates at its meeting in March, but remained sidelined in May. Under Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan, the Fed has never voted to either ease or tighten just once.
However, economists said the spread between real short-term interest rates and the target for the federal funds rate now was very narrow and may allow abstention.
"Everything out to the five-year note was doing well" at late afternoon, said Michael McClure, a trading manager at Zions First National Bank Capital Markets.
McClure said some shortening trades were likely responsible for the strong performance of bills versus coupons.

The stock market experienced sharp drops throughout much of the session and investors often seek refuge in the short end of the Treasury market in times of upheaval, where liquidity is plentiful and issues have the backing of the U.S. government.
"I'm not certain what stocks are suffering from, but (the falloff) was particularly potent today," said Carol Stone, senior economist at Nomura Securities International Inc.
She suspected a fall in the value of the dollar and technical factors were weighing on the market.
"Our view of the economy is a continuation of what we've had, low inflation and moderate growth," Stone said.
She said a news wire report of weaker third quarter earnings made little sense given current conditions.
Nonetheless, the Dow Jones Industrial Average closed 247 points lower.
"One of the things giving uncertainty to the economy is this UPS strike. On one hand it constrains the economy, but it also raises costs," Stone said. "It makes investors generally unhappy."
The Treasury's 30-year issue was ending down 1/32 at 97-22/32 to yield 6.55 percent.

At the short end of the maturity spectrum, three-month bills were down seven basis points to yield 5.12 percent. Six-month bills were also down seven basis points at 5.13 percent as were year bills were at 5.20 percent.
The 10-year issue was up 2/32 at 99-3/32 to yield 6.25 percent. The five-year was 5/32 higher at 99-23/32 to yield 6.07 percent and the two-year was 3/32 higher at 100-3/32 to yield 5.82 percent.
